discovery: Prediction and discovery of flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene (twistronics)

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics: two-dimensional van der Waals materials and moire quantum matter
motivation: Bistritzer and MacDonald (PNAS 2011) predicted that twisting two graphene sheets to a 'magic angle' near 1.1 degrees collapses the Dirac bands into nearly flat moire minibands, where interactions dominate. Jarillo-Herrero and co-workers (Nature 2018) realised this with a controlled tear-and-stack technique and discovered correlated insulating states and unconventional superconductivity in the same device, tunable by a gate. This turned the twist angle between atomic layers into a new, continuous design variable for quantum matter. The resulting field of moire materials has since produced orbital magnetism, quantised anomalous Hall states, fractional Chern insulators, moire excitons and sliding ferroelectricity across graphene and transition-metal dichalcogenide stacks. It is the clearest example of a simple structural degree of freedom in van der Waals crystals revealing a controllable physical mechanism, and it has reshaped condensed-matter physics and two-dimensional electronics worldwide.
